blocks.prompt: 3. Consider the arithmetico-geometric sequence defined by arithmetic part: \(a_{n+1} = 2n + 5\) and geometric part: \(b_{n-2} = \frac{1}{9}(-3)^{n}\). Find the \(n^{\text{th}}\) term and the sum of first three terms of the arithmetico-geometric sequence.
blocks.explanation:
The two parts are given with shifted subscripts (\(a_{n+1}\), \(b_{n-2}\)), not as \(a_n\) and \(b_n\).
Plan: shift each formula so the subscript becomes \(n\), multiply to get \(T_n\), then put \(n = 1, 2, 3\) and add.
steps:
Given: \(a_{n+1} = 2n + 5\), \(b_{n-2} = \frac{1}{9}(-3)^{n}\)
To find: \(T_n\) and \(T_1 + T_2 + T_3\).
Method: Replace \(n\) so that each subscript becomes \(n\); then \(T_n = a_n b_n\).

Get \(a_n\)
\[a_{(n-1)+1} = 2(n - 1) + 5\]
\[a_n = 2n - 2 + 5\]
\[a_n = 2n + 3\]
Why: Replacing \(n\) by \(n - 1\) everywhere turns the subscript \(n + 1\) into \(n\).

Write \(T_n\)
\[T_n = a_n b_n\]
\[= (2n + 3)(-3)^{n}\]
Why: The A.G.P. term is the product of the matching terms.

First three terms
\[T_1 = 5(-3) = -15\]
\[T_2 = 7(9) = 63\]
\[T_3 = 9(-27) = -243\]
Why: Put \(n = 1, 2, 3\); an odd power of \(-3\) is negative, an even power positive.

Add them
\[T_1 + T_2 + T_3\]
\[= -15 + 63 - 243\]
\[= 48 - 243 = -195\]
Why: Add from left to right.

Check with the given formulas
\[a_2 = 2(1) + 5 = 7 \;\checkmark\]
\[b_1 = \tfrac{1}{9}(-3)^{3} = -3 \;\checkmark\]
Why: Putting \(n = 1\) in \(a_{n+1}\) and \(n = 3\) in \(b_{n-2}\) gives the same values as our \(a_2 = 7\) and \(b_1 = -3\).
